answers.text:
The graph is show the percentage of household waste that recycled in three town between 1995 and 2020.

Firstly, in 1995 Hallowfield have 30 percent and it is the most high of the three. Marden is 12 percent and Trentbury is only 8 percent, so Trentbury is the lowest in this year. Secondly, after 2000 the Hallowfield start to go down. In 2010 it is 28 percent and in 2020 it is only 20 percent, so it lose many percent.

Thirdly, Marden and Trentbury is not same. They go up all the time. Marden go from 12 percent to 52 percent and this is a big increase. Trentbury also increase and in 2020 it become 61 percent, the most high number of the graph. Between 2005 and 2010 this two town pass the Hallowfield, because the people there don't want to recycle any more.

In my opinion recycling is very important for the environment and the government must help this town for more recycle.

why_this_band.task_response: There is no sentence that summarises the graph as a whole; the paragraphs simply read off figures in sequence, and the crossover point passes as a detail rather than being reported as a finding. The final paragraph adds a cause and an opinion that are not in the data (the government must help), which strays outside the task.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly pattern is mechanical and marks sequence rather than the logic of the paragraph content. The information is still presented in a trackable order, though, so the reader does not lose the thread.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Trend vocabulary stays limited to go up, go down, big increase and is repeated. Incorrect forms such as the most high and lose many percent slow the reader down.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Most sentences show subject–verb agreement or tense errors: is show, Hallowfield have, Marden go, this two town pass. Structures are almost entirely simple sentences; there is next to no subordination.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Drop the opinion in the final paragraph and replace it with a single sentence that states the overview of the graph (two towns rise, one falls), and write the whole report in the past tense.

answers.text:
The line graph shows the percentage of household waste which was recycled in three towns, Marden, Hallowfield and Trentbury, between 1995 and 2020.

Overall, two of the towns increased their recycling rate over the period, while the third one decreased. Trentbury and Marden ended much higher than they started, but Hallowfield finished lower than its first year.

In 1995, Hallowfield had the highest percentage with 30%, compared to 12% in Marden and only 8% in Trentbury. After that, Hallowfield rose a little to 33% in 2000, which was its highest point, and then it went down in every following year until it reached 20% in 2020.

Marden and Trentbury both showed a steady growth. Marden increased from 12% to 27% in 2005 and continued to 52% at the end of the period. Trentbury grew even faster, reaching 25% in 2005 and 61% in 2020, which was the highest figure of all three towns. Between 2005 and 2010 both of them passed Hallowfield, and in the same years Trentbury also became bigger than Marden.

In conclusion, the difference between the three towns was much larger in 2020 than it was in 1995.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview is clearly present in the second paragraph and figures are given for all three towns, with the crossover period identified. However, comparisons such as the gap widening from 22 points to 41 points go past without being backed up with numbers.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The paragraphing is logical: overview, the falling town, the rising towns, conclusion. Linking words are accurate but do not go beyond familiar patterns like After that / In conclusion.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is enough vocabulary for the task — highest point, steady growth, reached. In places such as became bigger than Marden and the third one decreased, the collocation does not quite settle.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses and time clauses are used, and most sentences are error-free. The remaining errors (a steady growth, in every following year) do not block meaning.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Name the percentage differences as points, and tie the closing sentence to a concrete figure such as from 22 to 41 points; this single change would move the task response up one band.

answers.text:
The line graph compares the proportion of household waste that was recycled in the towns of Marden, Hallowfield and Trentbury over the twenty-five years from 1995 to 2020.

Overall, recycling rates climbed steeply in two of the three towns while Hallowfield moved in the opposite direction, and the gap between the best and the worst performer widened considerably over the period.

In 1995 Hallowfield was comfortably ahead of its neighbours, recycling 30% of its household waste, roughly two and a half times the figure for Marden and almost four times that of Trentbury, which stood at just 8%. Hallowfield's rate edged up to a peak of 33% in 2000, but it then fell steadily for the remaining twenty years, ending at 20%.

Trentbury, by contrast, saw the most dramatic transformation. Having started from the lowest position, it overtook Marden between 2005 and 2010 and finished at 61%, a rise of more than fifty percentage points. Marden followed a similar though gentler upward path, more than quadrupling its rate from 12% to 52%. Both towns passed Hallowfield during the second half of the 2000s.

By 2020, therefore, the original ranking had been completely reversed, and the spread between the highest and lowest figures had widened from 22 to 41 percentage points.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview states both the direction and the outcome (the gap widening), and every town is supported with selected figures. The reversal of the ranking is given as a separate finding in the closing statement.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Information is grouped in a meaningful order — the falling town first, then the rising ones — rather than town by town. Linkers such as by contrast and therefore do real work in the sentence rather than acting as filler.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items such as edged up, peak, quadrupling, spread, percentage points appear with the right collocation. Choices like comfortably ahead sound natural.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: A participle structure (Having started from...), relative clauses and the past perfect are used under control. Errors are rare and do not stop the reader; even so, this is not the full flexibility of band 9.

answers.what_would_lift_it: At this level, progress is about precision rather than detail: add a measure that also gives the rate of change for each town (for example, an annual average).
